title: Emergent de Sitter Space and Non-Unitary Tensor Networks from Non-Hermitian Quantum Criticality
abstract: Extending the holographic principle to de Sitter (dS) spacetimes remains one of the most vital open frontiers in quantum gravity, where a microscopic, bottom-up tensor-network framework that relates boundary quantum data to emergent de Sitter spacetime is still lacking. In this work, we first show the emergence of de Sitter spacetime from boundary entanglement by formulating a non-unitary continuous multi-scale entanglement renormalization ansatz (cMERA) for a concrete non-Hermitian critical fermion chain. Within this emergent spacetime, we analyze the associated geodesics and show that they act as extremal Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces undergoing a smooth timelike-to-null transition. Remarkably, we demonstrate that this continuum trajectory dictates a distinct tensor-network architecture in which the bond-counting contribution naturally truncates at the discrete timelike-to-null transition toward the deep infrared. In the resulting architecture, the null ray along the horizon is represented by zero-cost links, since the associated cut severs no tensor legs. This network structure successfully reproduces the logarithmic scaling of non-unitary critical entanglement entropy, offering a bond-counting picture for the de Sitter RT formula. Our results provide the long-sought dS/(c)MERA correspondence at the level of both emergent spacetime and discrete holographic entanglement.
summary: The paper develops a novel tensor-network approach to realize the holographic principle in de Sitter space, moving beyond the established Anti-de Sitter framework. By applying non-unitary continuous MERA to a critical fermion chain, the authors show that entanglement structure naturally encodes an emergent dS geometry. This establishes a bottom-up dictionary (dS/cMERA) by showing how extremal surfaces map onto zero-cost links in the tensor network skeleton.
main_problem: The primary challenge is extending the holographic principle, which relates boundary entanglement to bulk geometry (like AdS/CFT), to de Sitter (dS) spacetimes by developing a microscopic tensor-network framework.
main_result: The authors establish a bottom-up dS/(c)MERA correspondence, demonstrating that non-unitary continuous MERA applied to a critical fermion chain yields an emergent de Sitter spacetime whose entanglement entropy scales correctly with the extremal surface length.
method: The work combines concepts from quantum information theory (MERA/tensor networks), condensed matter physics (non-Hermitian criticality), and general relativity (dS geodesics) by mapping continuum geometric quantities onto discrete bond-counting rules.
model_or_system: The model is a non-Hermitian critical fermion chain, analyzed using the continuous Multi-Scale Entanglement Renormalization Ansatz (cMERA). This system exhibits criticality that leads to an emergent Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime geometry in its holographic dual.
key_observables: Non-unitary critical entanglement entropy ($S \propto i \ln l$), extremal Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces, and the resulting dS metric components.
important_parameters: The non-Hermitian coupling parameters ($\mu$) defining criticality; the scale renormalization parameter $u$; and the geometric constants related to the de Sitter curvature ($\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that a bottom-up tensor network description can capture the physics of dS holography, requiring the use of biorthogonal structures due to non-Hermiticity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the embedding of the cMERA circuit into the de Sitter Penrose diagram and show how the extremal geodesic path corresponds to a specific zero-cost continuation (null link) within the tensor network structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reviewing AdS/CFT holography via MERA, then generalizing this framework to non-Hermitian systems to address dS space. The core is establishing the continuum metric from entanglement flow and subsequently deriving the discrete bond-counting rules that reproduce the expected logarithmic scaling for the dS extremal surface.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, calculable mechanism (bond counting) to connect quantum information concepts (MERA) directly to fundamental aspects of quantum gravity (dS holography), which is highly relevant for theoretical physicists studying emergent spacetime structures from microscopic degrees of freedom.
